package: MATCH-V1B: a task WITHOUT a place (remote, or without an approximate point) is sent in WAVES (first 300, then 1,000 workers every 30 minutes, until 5 active applications cover its open slots or the task is agreed/cancelled, at most 10,000 per task revision); ONE database transaction (one tick) notifies at most 1,000 workers in all (each notified worker holds two advisory locks of the shared lock table, about 4,800 entries on DEV), so a larger wave of a task WITH a place is sent in chunks of at most 1,000 per tick; an optional per-worker daily cap of new-task notifications (default OFF = 1000). Five NEW private functions (worker_notify_room_v1b, candidate_profile_ids_v1b, remote_wave_candidates_v1b, dispatch_config_v1b, dispatch_remote_wave_v1b), ONE REPLACED body (private.dispatch_next_wave, MATCH-V1 0bd8b64a -> d3cdfe2b) and eight new keys in the one data row private.marketplace_config 'match_v1_dispatch'. The ladder (mode LADDER) is untouched. No table, column, constraint, trigger, policy, index or grant on an existing object changed.

The README of the package, written before the standing order, still says the owner's exact word 'PRIMENI MATCH-V1B' is needed; the standing order replaced that default for proven packages. The daily cap stays OFF and the ladder stays off; both are his word.

method.statement: candidate.in-transaction.sql sent byte-exact through the connector's apply_migration (the connector adds its own transaction and the ledger insert). The statement was typed into the connector byte-exact (48,312 bytes, two non-ASCII characters, the z-caron in the notification title 'moze', that text is MATCH-V1's own and was left as pinned) and the stored statement was read back from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations afterwards: 1 statement, 48310 characters (48312 bytes), md5 5704ddb81d36c2936be0f709dd90a769, equal to the md5 of the file. The working-tree file and the committed blob are LF-only (0 CR), identical to what CI applied.
method.insideTheStatement: Pre-guards in the same transaction: certificate ready; none of the five new functions present and none of the eight new keys in the row (MATCH_V1B_ALREADY_OR_PARTIALLY_APPLIED); MATCH-V1 present; the 12 dependency body md5 pins; the predecessor body md5 of private.dispatch_next_wave; the dispatch row a valid MATCH-V1 row. The replacement: preimage md5, md5 of the new body against the generator's value, exactly one anchor of the old body in pg_get_functiondef, then the whole pg_proc row apart from the body and the function comment asserted unchanged. Post-guards: the five new bodies pinned by md5 with security definer, volatility, owner postgres, search_path=pg_catalog and ACL {postgres=X/postgres}; the replaced body pinned; the 12 dependencies unchanged; the row equal to before plus exactly the eight new keys; the defaults present; the knobs valid; both closure digests equal before and after (a temporary table of the pre-apply digests) and the certificate ready. Any difference aborts and rolls back.

revert.effect: revert.sql restores the MATCH-V1 body of private.dispatch_next_wave byte for byte, drops the five new functions and removes the eight keys from the row (every other value stays; lower the ceiling to 1,000 or less first). Code and configuration rollback only: deliveries, events, rounds and notifications already written stay.

notProven: No remote wave, no chunk and no budget deferral has run on DEV data yet (no open task without a place; 5 active worker profiles).

Whether the push provider delivers thousands of pushes in time is not measured and V1B does not touch the push transport: the existing sender sends about one push per minute (rpc_claim_push_transport claims one attempt per call), so a wave of 1,000 needs about 17 hours to leave the push queue and a notification expires after 24 hours; the in-app notification is immediate. A batch claim, a fair order between tasks and a queue-age metric are a separate package (PUSH-KAPACITET) that must precede any push.
The 40,000-worker load numbers (a wave of 1,000 in about 1.3 s, flat from the first to the last wave) come from a disposable server; CI hardware varies by about 1.5x.
The notification title still says 'Vam' (formal) in MATCH-V1's function body; the wording rule 'ti' is a separate, tiny text package.
followUps: PUSH-KAPACITET (batch claim in rpc_claim_push_transport, fair order between tasks, queue-age metric) before any push is switched on.

A text-only package: the notification title 'Nova prilika koja može da Vam odgovara' -> 'ti' voice (private.dispatch_next_wave and private.dispatch_remote_wave_v1b both carry it; pins must be regenerated).
workerDailyCap stays 1000 (off) until the owner chooses a number; the switch scripts switch-remote-waves-off.sql / -on.sql are in the folder and each is one guarded update.
The production Supabase project (a NEW project, decision R04) needs MATCH-V1, MATCH-V1B and the B24 candidates applied before its first real user.

afterApplyConfig.statement: one guarded UPDATE of the one row private.marketplace_config 'match_v1_dispatch': ceiling 1000 -> 10000, only where mode was ALL, ceiling 1000, owner 'MATCH-V1 2026-10-07', workerNotifyPerTransaction 1000 and remoteWaves true; run through execute_sql at 2026-10-07 23:01:22 UTC (a data change, not a migration, so no ledger row); the returned row passed private.dispatch_config_v1b (remoteWaves true, notifyBudget 1000, workerDailyCap off)
afterApplyConfig.why: the ceiling had been lowered from the owner's 10000 to 1000 on 2026-10-07 at 21:47 UTC because one transaction can notify only about 4,000 distinct workers (two advisory locks per notified worker). MATCH-V1B's per-transaction notify budget (1,000) and chunking remove that limit, so the ceiling the owner named is restored.
afterApplyConfig.note: mode stays ALL; the ladder is not switched on; the daily cap is OFF (1000). A task with a place and 10,000 matching workers is complete after ten ticks (one per minute); a task without a place reaches 10,000 workers in about five hours.
